features.name: Academic credential level
features.description: Captures the highest level of formal technical education the applicant presents.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree, equivalent, or no advanced degree is presented.
Master's degree is presented.
Doctoral degree is presented.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures direct experience designing agent-based systems with bounded autonomy, permissions, supervision, guardrails, or auditability.

levels.descriptor: No agentic systems experience is mentioned.
References agents in passing without clear ownership or design detail.
Describes a concrete agentic pipeline or tooling example.
Shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architecture, including boundaries, supervision, permissions, logging, or auditability.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures practical mastery of data structures and algorithms as demonstrated through concrete engineering examples or system improvements.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Claims strong data-structure or algorithm knowledge, but without a concrete example.
Gives at least one concrete example of improving a system through better algorithm or data-structure choice.
Uses a specific, nontrivial example to show strong algorithmic judgment and a meaningful systems improvement.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: Captures hands-on experience shipping AI or LLM-backed systems in production and treating reliability, evaluation, and failure modes seriously.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI or LLM exposure without concrete deployment detail.
Describes shipped AI features or workflows in production.
Describes shipped AI work plus evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or trustworthiness practices.

features.name: Collaboration orientation
features.description: Captures whether the letter emphasizes partnering with other engineers or security specialists and building for internal collaborators rather than working purely solo.

levels.descriptor: Does not signal collaboration with security specialists or users of the tooling.
Uses general teamwork or internal-customer language, but without much specificity.
Explicitly wants to work closely with security engineers, learn from domain specialists, or build in tight proximity to the teams served.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security tooling as helping developers and internal users adopt safer defaults with less friction.

levels.descriptor: Does not discuss the needs or behavior of developer users.
Mentions helping teams in generic terms.
Explicitly focuses on reducing friction or making the secure path easier for developers.
Shows clear empathy for busy engineers and explains adoption in terms of defaults, workflows, and usable tooling rather than process.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter substantiates claims with specific technical examples, mechanisms, named systems, or measurable details.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on generic claims or alignment statements.
Provides some concrete terms or examples but not enough to let the reader picture the work.
Uses several specific examples, mechanisms, or outcomes to support claims.
Is densely grounded in concrete evidence, with enough operational detail that the work feels tangible and credible.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how central and production-grade Go appears in the applicant's relevant engineering experience.

levels.descriptor: Go is absent or its use is unclear.
Go is mentioned, but not as a major language in the applicant's work.
Go is presented as a regular or important language for backend work.
Go is clearly described as a primary language or daily driver tied to substantial backend ownership.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter explains the practical outcomes or effects of the applicant's work on users, workflows, capacity, reliability, or security.

levels.descriptor: Lists tasks with no visible outcomes.
Hints at benefit but remains mostly activity-based.
States clear outcomes such as reduced manual work, faster systems, or fewer bugs.
Shows strong leverage language, tying work to capacity, attention saved, or meaningful organizational effect.

features.name: Maintainer mindset
features.description: Captures whether the applicant emphasizes maintenance, reliability, failure modes, inheritance, and long-term operability as core engineering concerns.

levels.descriptor: No clear maintenance or reliability philosophy is shown.
Uses general quality language, but without a distinct long-term ownership mindset.
Clearly values resilience, inherited systems, or careful long-lived engineering.
Strong maintainer ethos, such as upstream fixing, higher standards for security tooling, or repeated emphasis on quiet reliability and stewardship.

features.name: Narrative cohesion
features.description: Captures whether the letter forms a coherent, well-structured case for fit rather than reading like a disconnected checklist.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like disconnected bullets, fragments, or stacked claims.
The letter has some structure, but transitions or the overall arc are uneven.
The letter coherently links background, technical experience, and interest in the role.
The letter presents an especially well-shaped narrative that makes the applicant's trajectory and fit feel natural.

features.name: Narrative distinctiveness
features.description: Captures how memorable and individually voiced the letter feels, including distinctive framing or openings beyond generic application language.

levels.descriptor: Highly formulaic prose with little individual voice.
Competent but generic prose with only limited individuality.
Includes a memorable framing device, belief, or personal thesis.
Sustains a distinctive, authentic voice throughout while still serving the application's purpose.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures ongoing attacker-oriented security practice outside ordinary product work, such as CTFs or similar adversarial exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
Shows occasional or casual participation in CTFs or similar practice.
Shows sustained participation in CTFs or other regular adversarial practice.
Shows sustained adversarial practice with strong competitive results or clearly serious investment.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures responsibility for public codebases through upstream fixes, contributions, maintenance, releases, or other stewardship beyond the applicant's employer.

levels.descriptor: No open-source work is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional patches or fixes sent upstream.
The letter shows regular contribution or maintainership, including review or release responsibilities.
The letter shows stewardship of a broadly used project or community, with clear responsibility for releases, roadmap, or contributor management.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition, seriousness, and systems depth of self-directed projects outside the applicant's day job.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for foundational or shared infrastructure work whose impact compounds across many teams, products, or services.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work.
Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation.
Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams.
Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains.

features.name: Production engineering track record
features.description: Captures the breadth and depth of real production delivery experience shown through shipping, maintaining, testing, or owning production systems.

levels.descriptor: Meets the baseline only, with limited scope or a small number of launched systems described.
Shows a solid early-career record, with several years and some repeated launch or maintenance work.
Shows a strong mid-career record, with multiple launches and clear production breadth.
Presents an extensive record for this role, combining years, repeated launches, and broad responsibility across production systems.

features.name: Professional tenure
features.description: Captures the amount of relevant post-school professional software engineering experience the letter claims.

levels.descriptor: Claims roughly 2 to 3 years of relevant professional experience.
Claims roughly 4 to 5 years of relevant professional experience.
Claims 6 or more years of relevant professional experience.

features.name: Programming language breadth
features.description: Captures the range of additional programming languages the applicant presents beyond the core required stack.

levels.descriptor: No additional languages are mentioned.
Mentions 1 to 2 additional languages.
Mentions 3 to 5 additional languages.
Mentions more than 5 additional languages.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how central, substantial, and production-grade Python appears in the applicant's work on services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or only minimally mentioned.
Python is mentioned for light scripting or general familiarity.
Python is used regularly for tooling, automation, analysis, or services.
Python is presented as production-grade and central, with evidence of robust service or tooling development.

features.name: Role-specific motivation
features.description: Captures how clearly and convincingly the letter explains why this exact role or team fits the applicant and maps their background or motivation to it.

levels.descriptor: Shows generic interest in applying with little reason for this role in particular.
States interest in the role but with broad or familiar reasoning.
Gives a clear role-specific reason tied to security engineering, automation, or impact.
Articulates a distinctive and memorable rationale that tightly links prior experience to this exact mandate.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience assessing systems for security issues through review, threat modeling, attack-surface analysis, remediation validation, or similar methods.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.name: Security automation mission insight
features.description: Captures how specifically the letter shows understanding of the team's core problem as scaling security judgment through automation, triage, agents, and related workflows.

levels.descriptor: Frames the role generically as software or security work, with little sign of understanding the specific problem the team solves.
Mentions automation or security scale in broad terms, but without a crisp diagnosis of the underlying bottleneck.
Frames the work as reducing manual security workload or improving vulnerability handling at scale.
Articulates a precise thesis about the domain, such as scaling scarce expert judgment, treating vulnerability response as a systems problem, or multiplying one finding into fleet-wide protection.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: Captures the rigor and relevance of formal security certifications or other third-party security validation cited in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A baseline credential such as Security+ is presented.
A hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP is presented.

features.name: Security engineering mindset
features.description: Captures the maturity and rigor of the applicant's stated philosophy about secure engineering, including correctness, guardrails, and dependable security-critical systems.

levels.descriptor: Offers no distinct philosophy about the quality bar required for security engineering.
Makes only generic statements about reliability or security importance.
Expresses a clear philosophy of quiet resilience, dependable systems, or a higher standard for security tooling.
Builds a memorable, well-integrated case that security tooling demands exceptional rigor and ties that belief to prior work or design choices.

features.name: Vulnerability workflow automation
features.description: Captures direct ownership of tooling that automates vulnerability intake, triage, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related handling workflows.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not describe vulnerability-handling automation.
The letter mentions security automation in general, but not a specific vulnerability triage workflow.
The letter shows direct experience automating intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.
The letter shows a clear transformation of a manual vulnerability workflow or explicitly states operational impact from the automation.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures the surface correctness, proofreading quality, and overall mechanical professionalism of the letter.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors, misspellings, or naming mistakes noticeably distract from the application.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains readable.
Mostly clean writing with only minor slips.
Polished, professional, and essentially error-free throughout.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures idiosyncratic constructs that do not clearly recur enough to justify their own shared criterion.

levels.descriptor: No open-source involvement is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches, fixes, or upstream contributions.
Shows active maintenance of a library or project, including releases or outside users.
Shows sustained stewardship with reviews, releases, community interaction, and evidence that the project is meaningfully used by others.
